review_reference: Owner request of 2026-11-11 (D-Eminence, relayed by the coordinator in the admin dashboard contract): a super admin only activity dashboard (people, care activity, Migrate and Ask, a daily chart, the latest sign-ups and uploads) for 7, 30 or 90 days, with names shortened ("Ada O."), emails masked ("a***@gmail.com") and Health IDs shortened ("HID-7K…M9") inside the database, and every view audited. Numbered 0123: 0109-0121 are held by open pull requests, 0122 by the collect sign-up fields plan, and the coordinator reserved 0123 for this. Unsigned: reviewed_by is empty until the owner signs. SIGNED by the owner, D-Eminence, in chat on 2026-11-11 (~01:05 UTC): "0123 signed", after the adversarial review's four findings (file-name privacy x2, policy locks, daily counts) were fixed at 890ded5b.
evidence: Single migration 0123_admin_platform_activity.sql, unsigned until the owner signs (reviewed_by is empty). WHAT IT DOES (additive only; no existing table, column, row, policy or function body changes): (1) the permission platform.dashboard.read, granted to platform_super_admin and to no other role; (2) identity.admin_platform_activity(integer) returns jsonb, SECURITY DEFINER, VOLATILE, search_path pinned, EXECUTE for hid_identity_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime only: 42501 ADMIN_PERMISSION_DENIED unless the session account holds platform.dashboard.read, 22023 ADMIN_INVALID_DAYS unless 7, 30 or 90, one platform audit row per call (action admin.overview.activity.read, details {"days": n} only), the sealed demo tenant left out of every number and list, names, emails and Health IDs shortened in SQL, and no part of an upload's file name returned: only its kind from an allowlist of the last extension (pdf -> PDF; jpg, jpeg, png, heic, tif, tiff -> Image; docx -> Word; anything else -> Document); the immutable name shortener and file-kind label granted to no role; daily[] and activeInPeriod from one grouped pass over auth.sessions and one over identity.patients joined to the days, not a pass per day; (3) a read window for production's non-BYPASSRLS owner: the table identity.admin_activity_read_windows (RLS enabled, no policy, no grant), the helper identity.admin_activity_read_open() (granted to no role) and (last, section 4) one permissive SELECT policy TO the applier role only on each of the eleven FORCE row-level-security tables the read counts (ehr.encounters, clinical_notes, vitals, diagnoses, prescriptions, lab_requests, documents, document_scan_events, staff_chat_messages, ocr.publications, outreach.registration_cases), true only while the function holds a window row for its own backend and transaction (inserted after the permission check, deleted before the audit row). No runtime role is a member of the applier, so no runtime query evaluates these policies. Old services: nothing calls the function until the Identity API image with GET /api/v1/admin/overview/activity is deployed. SUITE: services/ehr-api/test/database/admin-platform-activity.integration.sql, 40 cases, rollback-only: who may call (platform_admin, operations admin, disabled super admin, no subject and a patient refused; the super admin accepted), the days accepted, the audit rows, the read window not forgeable by the runtime and closed after each call, the eleven policies, the counts moved by synthetic fixtures, the daily sign-ups adding up to newInPeriod, the shortened values (no whole name, email or Health ID, and no part of a file name, in the answer) and the file kind for 18 names including 'HIV_test.pdf', 'HIVpos9.pdf', 'Ada.Okonkwo', 'x.pdf.exe', 'scan.HIVpositive' and 'letter.doc'. Proved on a throwaway local PostgreSQL 16 twice: 0001-0108 + 0123 applied by a superuser (with all 82 database suites passing), and 0001-0108 + 0123 applied by a non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS migrator with MIGRATION_TARGET=rds (the suite passes 40/40; with three of the policies dropped it fails 3o, 5d and 6e, so the window is what lets the production owner count). LOCKS (pg_locks before commit, 0123 applied in one transaction with lock_timeout 5s on a copy at 0001-0108): ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on ehr.clinical_notes, ehr.diagnoses, ehr.document_scan_events, ehr.documents, ehr.encounters, ehr.lab_requests, ehr.prescriptions, ehr.staff_chat_messages, ehr.vitals, ocr.publications and outreach.registration_cases (CREATE POLICY), none of them held before section 4 (checked: 0 before it), taken there in one LOCK TABLE ... IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE NOWAIT in that fixed order, retried every 10 ms for at most 5 s, then 55P03 '0123: a table that gets a read-window policy stayed busy for 5 seconds; run the release again later'; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the new identity.admin_activity_read_windows and its key; ROW EXCLUSIVE on auth.permissions and auth.role_permissions (two inserted rows); ACCESS SHARE or ROW SHARE on auth.accounts, auth.roles, identity.patients, identity.registration_cases, ehr.documents_effective, ehr.imported_attachment_scan_events and platform.commercial_products, and catalog locks. APPLY TIME: 27 ms in all, 21 ms from section 4 (the eleven locks) to the end of the post-checks. BUSY TABLE: with another session holding ROW EXCLUSIVE on ehr.vitals for 7 s the apply stopped with that 55P03 after about 5 s and nothing applied, and a read of ehr.encounters during the retries answered in 20 ms (a NOWAIT attempt never queues and a failed one releases what it took); with ehr.vitals held for 4 s the apply waited and then succeeded. COST (seeded throwaway database, 2,000,000 auth.sessions over a year across 50,000 accounts and 500,000 identity.patients, analyzed, called as hid_identity_api_runtime): days=7 1.2 s, days=30 1.5 s, days=90 2.6 s for the whole function, under the Identity API's 15 s statement_timeout; the previous per-day daily[] alone took 99.4 s at days=90 on the same data. INDEXES: none added. auth.sessions has no index on issued_at or last_used_at (only (family_id, issued_at) and its account index), and identity.patients and ehr.documents none on created_at alone, so these are sequential scans whose cost grows with the tables, not the days asked for; the clinical tables' created_at indexes all lead with another column.
